2024_195_course_description_book_2024_20.paragraph: The Troy School District 2024-2025 Course Description Book, revised January 2024 under Superintendent Dr. Richard Machesky, catalogs the courses offered at Athens High School and Troy High School together with graduation requirements, nondiscrimination policy, and Oakland Schools Technical Campus options. All students must earn a total of 22.5 credits to be eligible for a Troy High School or Troy Athens diploma, including 4.0 credits of English, 4.0 of mathematics, 3.0 of science, 3.0 of social studies, and 3.0 in the combined World Language / Fine & Applied Arts / CTE category. Beginning with the class of 2028, 0.5 credit of Personal Finance is embedded into Economics as a graduation requirement.
2024_195_course_description_book_2024_20.page:
**Document type and origin**
Course Descriptions for Athens High School and Troy High School, 2024-2025, issued by the Troy School District under Dr. Richard Machesky, Superintendent of Schools, and marked "Revised, January 2024." Before the Board of Education on February 27, 2024. The closing page credits the Department of Teaching & Learning, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, 248.823.5221.

**Buildings and contacts**

| School | Principal | Address | Main Office | Counseling |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Athens High School | Mr. Vernon Burden | 4333 John R. Road, Troy, MI 48085 | 248.823.2900 | 248.823.2962 |
| Troy High School | Mr. Remo Roncone | 4777 Northfield Parkway, Troy, MI 48098 | 248.823.2700 | 248.823.2715 |

Athens fax 248.823.2913 and attendance 248.823.2901; Troy High fax 248.823.2713 and attendance 248.823.2701.

**Nondiscrimination**
Cites Title IX of the Educational Amendments of 1972, Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, and the Americans with Disabilities Act. Jordan M. Harris, J.D., Assistant Superintendent of Employee Services, is named Title IX and Section 504/ADA Coordinator for employment and personnel matters; the Director of Special Education serves that role for students. Questions go to John Pagel, Assistant Superintendent of Employee Services, 4400 Livernois Road, Troy, MI 48098-4799, (248)823-4000.

**Graduation requirements (classes of 2025, 2026, 2027, 2028)**

| Area | Credits |
| --- | --- |
| English | 4.0 |
| Mathematics | 4.0 |
| Science | 3.0 |
| Social Studies | 3.0 |
| World Language / Fine & Applied Arts / CTE | 3.0 |
| Physical Education | 1.0 |
| Health | 0.5 |
| VPAA | 1.0 |
| Personal Finance | 0.5 |
| Online Learning Experience | 0.0 |
| State Assessments | 0.0 |
| Total credits needed for graduation | 22.5 |

Science for the classes of 2027 and 2028 is Biology 1.0, Chemistry 0.5 plus Physics 0.5, Environmental Science: Human Impact 0.5, and a Science Elective 0.5; the classes of 2025 and 2026 take Biology 1.0, Chemistry OR Physics 1.0, and a Science Elective 1.0. The World Language column requires 2.0 credits of World Language (non-sequential accepted), or 1.0 World Language credit plus either 1.0 CTE credit or 1.0 VPAA credit. The online learning requirement is a 20-hour non-credit experience embedded across middle and high school.

**Flexibility options** (updated 9.2015, MCL 380.1278a & MCL 380.1278b)
Personal Curriculum aligned to a student's Educational Development Plan; automatic waiver of the 0.5 Physical Education elective for 2 seasons of district athletics or marching band; World Language flexibility for heritage language proficiency, international study, or CTE/VPAA substitution; and CTE program completion exchanged 1:1 for science, world language, or Algebra 2 credit.

**Departments covered**
Business; Career Technical Education; Industrial Technical; Life Skills; English; English Language Development; Visual Arts; Fine Arts; Music; Theatre Arts; Health; Mathematics; Media; Physical Education; Science; Social Studies; Special Education; and World Language (French, Spanish, Japanese, Chinese, German), benchmarked to the ACTFL Proficiency Guidelines.

**Oakland Schools Technical Campus**
OSTC-SE at 5055 Delemere Street, Royal Oak (north of 14 Mile between Crooks and Coolidge), plus a Northeast Campus in Pontiac. Grades 11-12; course numbers 08101 Session 1 AM and 08102 Session 2 PM. Morning classes begin 7:50 AM and dismiss 10:20 AM; afternoon classes begin 12:00 PM and dismiss 2:30 PM. OSTC generally recommends 1.5 credits per semester; where regular students carry six (6) credits, OSTC students carry three (3) at the home high school and three (3) at OSTC. Apply online at www.ostconline.com by the end of February. Credits offered at OSTC are not NCAA approved.

**Anti-discrimination grievance procedure**
Written grievances go to the Assistant Superintendent of Employee Services, the designated compliance administrator, within 10 workdays of the incident, with escalating deadlines through Step 2 (Assistant Superintendent or Deputy Superintendent) and Step 3 (Superintendent), whose written answer is final and binding.
2024_195_course_description_book_2024_20.verbose:
**Identification.** "2024-2025 Course Descriptions for Athens High School and Troy High School," issued by the Troy School District over the name of Dr. Richard Machesky, Superintendent of Schools, and marked "Revised, January 2024." The version before the Board of Education is dated February 27, 2024. The back page carries the Department of Teaching & Learning, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, 248.823.5221.

**Policy of nondiscrimination.** The opening statement recites Title IX of the Educational Amendments of 1972, Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, and the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA). Jordan M. Harris, J.D., Assistant Superintendent of Employee Services, is appointed Title IX and Section 504/ADA Coordinator for employment and personnel matters; the District's Director of Special Education is the Section 504/ADA Coordinator for handicapped and suspected handicapped students. Questions are directed to John Pagel, Assistant Superintendent of Employee Services, Troy School District, 4400 Livernois Road, Troy, MI 48098-4799, (248)823-4000.

**Building directory.** Athens High School, Mr. Vernon Burden, Principal, 4333 John R. Road, Troy, Michigan 48085: main office 248.823.2900, fax 248.823.2913, counseling 248.823.2962, attendance 248.823.2901. Troy High School, Mr. Remo Roncone, Principal, 4777 Northfield Parkway, Troy, Michigan 48098: main office 248.823.2700, fax 248.823.2713, counseling 248.823.2715, attendance 248.823.2701.

**Graduation requirements, classes of 2025, 2026, 2027 and 2028.** English 4.0 credits (English 9 - 1.0; English 10 - 1.0 for the class of 2028+; English 11 Lit/Comp plus an English elective or 11 English AP 1 & 2 - 1.0; English 12 Lit/Comp 1 & 2 or 12 English AP 1 & 2 - 1.0). Science 3.0 credits, structured differently by cohort: the classes of 2027 and 2028 take Biology 1.0, Chemistry 0.5 and Physics 0.5, Environmental Science: Human Impact 0.5, and a Science Elective 0.5, while the classes of 2025 and 2026 take Biology 1.0, Chemistry OR Physics 1.0, and a Science Elective 1.0. Mathematics 4.0 credits (Algebra 1 - 1.0; Geometry - 1.0; Algebra 2 or Algebra 2 Part A & Part B - 1.0, which may be met through CTE program completion such as OSTC; Math Elective - 1.0), with a math experience required in the final year of high school. Social Studies 3.0 credits (World History/Geography 1 & 2 - 1.0; American History/Geography 1 & 2 - 1.0; Economics - 0.5; Government and Civics - 0.5). Personal Finance 0.5 credit, embedded into Economics and a graduation requirement beginning with the class of 2028, earned through a TSD Economics or AP Economics course. Physical Education 1.0 credit (Intro to Physical Activity 0.5 plus a P.E. elective 0.5). Health 0.5 credit. VPAA 1.0 credit, covering Industrial Technology, Business and Life Skills classes. World Language, Fine & Applied Arts, CTE 3.0 credits: 2.0 credits of World Language (non-sequential accepted), or 1.0 World Language credit plus either 1.0 CTE or 1.0 VPAA credit. Online Learning Experience 0.0 credit, a 20-hour requirement embedded in Troy classroom experiences. State Assessments 0.0. Credit-bearing high school courses taken before matriculation appear on the Troy transcript with grades earned. Total credits needed for graduation: 22.5.

**Flexibility options** (updated 9.2015, citing MCL 380.1278a and MCL 380.1278b). Personal Curriculum allows additional core credits in lieu of other requirements when aligned to the student's Educational Development Plan (EDP). Students completing 2 seasons of Troy School District athletics or 2 seasons of marching band are excused from the 0.5 credit Physical Education elective through an automated transcript process requiring no forms. The 2.0 World Language credit requirement may flex for non-English heritage language proficiency, international study and residence, or CTE/VPAA substitution, documented by a Personal Curriculum. CTE program completion exchanges credits 1:1 for science, world language, or the Algebra 2 requirement.

**Business Department.** Accounting 1 (005002), Accounting 2 (005022) and Financial Management (005122); Business Law + Management, Digital Business (Microsoft Office Specialist certification, Wordpress, Canva, AI ethics), Business Entrepreneurship, Web Creation 1 and Web Page Creation 2. Junior Business Field Study (Co-op) requires 10+ credits for junior status and Senior Business Field Study (Co-op) requires 14.5+ credits for senior status, granting up to 2.0 credits for work experience of at least 10 hours per week and 200 hours per semester. Marketing offerings are Marketing (005222), Marketing 2, Honors Marketing (preparing students for the Principles of Marketing CLEP examination), Sports and Entertainment Marketing with a Troy Athens Fantasy League, School Based Enterprise (12th grade only), and Marketing Field Study (Co-op) worth up to 2.0 credits.

**Career Technical Education.** Careers in Education 1 (007393) and Careers in Education 2 (007403), tied to the Troy Athens Preschool, offer advanced placement credit at Central University, Western Michigan University, Oakland University, Macomb Community College and Davenport University and eligibility for the Child Development Associate (CDA) credential. Hospitality/Food Services is built around the renovated Terrace Café restaurant lab at Athens: Restaurant Operations / Terrace Cafe (007384, 2 hours, 2 credits), Commercial Baking (007373) and Commercial Foods (007473), all using the ProStart curriculum with ServSafe Sanitation Certificate eligibility. Troy High automotive courses Automotive Technology 1 through 4 meet NATEF Automotive Maintenance and Light Repair standards, with Automotive Tech 2 (107294/207294) a 2-hour block. Woodworking Design & Fabrication 1, 2 and 3 use CAD, CNC and 3D printing.

**Industrial Technical Department.** Mechatronics 1 (108713/208713) and Mechatronics 2 (CADD/CAM, robotics, sensors, fluid power; recommended for Robotics Club), Architectural Drawing 1 and 2, and Game Design 1 and 2 at Athens, primarily using Java and mobile platforms.

**Life Skills Department.** Parenthood/Child Development 1 and 2, both eligible for advanced placement credit at Oakland Community College; Essential Skills for Adulthood; Personal Money Management; Foods and Culture and Foods 2 at Troy High; Fashion Design 1 and 2; Stitchery; and Interior Design/CAD using Auto CAD.

**English Department.** Core sequence: 101043/201043 English 9, 101053/201053 English 10, 000821 11 English Literature/Composition, 100443 11 English AP 1, 200443 11 English AP 2, 100113/200113 12 English Lit/Comp, and 100453/200453 12 English AP 1 & 2. Electives include Creative Writing 1 and 2, Classical Mythology and Drama, Film and Literature, Literature of Suspense, Science Fiction, Voices in Literature, Sports Literature, Personal Communication, Speech 1 and 2, Debate 1 and 2, Modern Shakespeare, Writing for Publication in Journalism, Newspaper and Yearbook strands, Writing for Broadcasting and Advanced Writing for Broadcasting, Advanced Publication Production, Seminar AP, and Research AP (002533), which culminates in an academic paper of approximately 4000-5000 words with an oral defense.

**English Language Development.** Initial placement follows the State of Michigan Entrance Protocol, with annual WIDA ACCESS administration. Courses are Beginner ELD (101013/201013), Intermediate ELD, Advanced ELD, Bridges to Lit/Comp for ELs, and EL Tutorial (pass/fail). Language Support content classes cover LS Biology, LS Chemistry, LS Physics, LS World History/Geography 1 and 2, LS American History/Geography 1 and 2, LS Government/Civics, and LS Economics.

**Visual and Fine Arts.** Multi-Media Art, Mindful Art, Drawing 1 and Advanced Drawing, Painting 1 and Advanced Painting, Cartoons, Comics & Animation, Ceramics 1 and Advanced Ceramics, Lettering & Calligraphy, Studio Art (106373/206373), Advanced Art AP (106393/206393), Applied Arts and Design, Computer Graphics 1 and Advanced Computer Graphics, Sculpture, Principles of Photography 1 (007112) and Advanced Photography (007114).

**Music and Theatre Arts.** Campus, Concert, Cadet (Troy High) and Symphonic Bands; Jazz Ensemble, Jazz Explorations, Color Guard and Percussion; Freshman, Concert, Symphony and Philharmonic (Troy High) Orchestras; Treble Choir, Concert Choir, Mixed Chorus (Athens), Madrigal Singers (Athens) and Chorus/Choir Accompanist; AP Music Theory (106053/206053), which counts as a math elective credit for seniors who have completed all other required math credits; and Intro to Music Technology and Recording using ProTools. Theatre offerings are Theatre I, II and III plus Youth Theatre.

**Health Department.** 008852 Health, required for graduation, covering healthy lifestyles, violence, sexual harassment, nutrition, fitness and weight control, alcohol and drug abuse, tobacco, human sexuality, birth control and sexually transmitted diseases including HIV/AIDS; and 008573 Peer Mediation for grade 12.

**Mathematics Department.** Algebra 1, Intensified Algebra 1 (103123/203123, a double-blocked 2-hour course), Geometry, Geometry Honors, Algebra 2 Part A and Part B, Algebra 2, Algebra 2 Honors, Precalculus, Precalculus Honors, College Algebra, Calculus AB AP, Calculus BC AP, Statistics AP, Calculus 3 (003212) and Linear Algebra (003222) offered as Dual Enrollment through Lawrence Tech, AP Computer Science A in Java, Computer Science Principles AP, Cybersecurity (003172 at THS, 103172/203172 at AHS), and Introduction to Data Science (103383/203383) using the Pyret programming platform.

**Media Department.** Media Center Services, Media Center Techniques, Innovation Learning (008682) and Innovation Lab (008692), influenced by the "D school" at Stanford University and referencing creatinginnovators.com and dschool.stanford.edu, plus Seminar AP and Research AP.

**Physical Education.** 007952 Intro to Physical Activity (Level 1) and 007962 Intro to Physical Activity (Level 2), one of which is required for graduation and includes CPR training, physical fitness, swimming testing and team sports. Other offerings include Exercise and Lifelong Fitness, Self Defense and Lifelong Fitness, Net Sports & Fitness, Fall and Spring Team Sports & Fitness, Weight Training and Aerobics, Tumbling & Gymnastics/Fitness, Learning to Swim, Strength and Conditioning, and Lifeguarding/Advanced Swimming (005522), which requires students to be 15 years old and carries a $40 Red Cross certification cost. The President's Challenge Physical Fitness Test is given in most physical education classes.

**Science Department.** Biology (104003/204003), Anatomy and Physiology with dissections culminating in a shark experience and a cat dissection, Genetics/Bacteriology/Biotechnology/Embryology (104063/204063, covering CRISPR, PCR, RFLPs and gel electrophoresis), Biology AP, Chemistry 1 (004122) and Chemistry 2 (004123), AP Chemistry, Organic Chemistry, Physics 1 (004231) and Physics 2 (004232), Engineering Physics, AP Physics, Physics C AP, Environmental Science: Human Impact (004314), Astronomy, Forensic Science, and Environmental Science AP (104273/204273), which satisfies the Earth Science requirement.

**Social Studies Department.** 002232 World History/Geography 1 (collapse of Rome through the French Revolution and defeat of Napoleon), Human Geography AP, 102023 American History/Geography 1 and 202023 American History/Geography 2 (United States from 1877), American History/Geography AP, 002062 Economics, Economics AP, 002072 Government and Civics, Government AP, 002242 World History/Geography 2 (Industrial Revolution to current issues), World History/Geography AP, Psychology 1 and 2, Psychology AP, Sociology, Mental Health, Philosophy, Comparative Government and Politics AP built on China, Great Britain, Iran, Mexico, Nigeria and Russia, Political Science, History of American Criminal Law, History through Film, Conflicts of the 20th & 21st Centuries, Introduction to Leadership, Leadership Lab, LINK, 106383/206383 AP Art History covering 250 works of art, and 002617 Stories of Yourself & Others, a grade 12 interdisciplinary course carrying 0.5 ELA credit and 0.5 History credit.

**Special Education Department.** Achievement Skills 1A (109909) and 1B (209909) for 9th grade through Achievement Skills 4A (109912) and 4B (209912) for 12th grade; Linguistics 2D, 2E and 2F; Reading Strategies; Integrated Math 1 and 2; English Language Arts 1 and 2; Math Skills A/B; and Life Skills Math. All are for students certified by an IEPT, with placement made in collaboration with the IEP case manager; Central Office Special Education is reached at 248.823.5096.

**World Language Department.** French, Spanish, Japanese, Chinese and German are each offered at levels 1 through 4 plus an AP course (for example French 1 at 100603/200603 and French AP at 100643/200643; Spanish AP at 100733/200733; Japanese AP at 108863/208863; Chinese AP at 100813/200813; German runs 100653/200653 through 100683/200683). Japanese 2 adds 120 basic Kanji characters, Japanese 3 another 170+ Kanji, and Japanese 4 another 180+ Kanji. Levels are benchmarked to the ACTFL Proficiency Guidelines, from Novice-mid/Novice-high at level 1 to Intermediate-high/Advanced-low at AP, with Advanced Placement examinations given in May.

**Oakland Schools Technical Campus.** OSTC-SE is at 5055 Delemere Street, Royal Oak, Michigan (north of 14 Mile between Crooks and Coolidge), with a Northeast Campus in Pontiac, Michigan. Programs are offered to juniors and seniors on a selective basis under course numbers 08101 Session 1 AM and 08102 Session 2 PM. Morning session classes begin at 7:50 AM and are dismissed at 10:20 AM; afternoon session classes begin at 12:00 PM and are dismissed at 2:30 PM. OSTC recommends high school credit based on local district requirement, generally 1.5 credits per semester; if regular students carry six (6) credits, OSTC students must carry three (3) credits at their home high school in addition to three (3) credits at OSTC. Programs include Automotive Technology and Cosmetology (both must begin in 11th grade), Collision Repair and Refinishing, Computer Programming, Computer Networking, Construction Technology, Culinary Arts/Hospitality, Electrical and Energy Technologies, Entrepreneurship & Advanced Marketing, Health Sciences, Machining, Mechatronics, Visual Imaging Technology, Welding, and Homeland Security (Criminal Justice or Cyber Security). A bus transports students to OSTC-SE, while afternoon-session students provide their own transportation home. Applications are made online at www.ostconline.com by the end of February. Credits offered at OSTC are not NCAA approved.

**Anti-discrimination grievance procedure.** Grievances may be filed on the basis of sex (including sexual harassment), race, color, religion, national origin, age (employees only), height, weight, marital status, or handicap, in writing to the Assistant Superintendent of Employee Services, the designated compliance administrator. Step 1 requires filing within 10 workdays of the incident, a copy to the Assistant Superintendent not later than the next workday, a meeting within 5 workdays of the filing date, and a written answer within 3 workdays of the meeting. Step 2 allows appeal within 3 workdays, a meeting within 10 workdays of receipt of the appeal, and a written answer within 5 workdays. Step 3 escalates to the Superintendent on the same workday schedule, and the Superintendent's written answer is final and binding on all parties. Grievances not filed or appealed within the time limits are deemed abandoned, and records are treated confidentially.
